pages.excerpt:
2.2. Bootstrapping Methods
In real life, bonds don’t always pay at clean, regular intervals.
Bootstrapping gives a simple way to build the yield curve step-by-step
from market prices.
• We start with short-term instruments like Treasury bills to estimate
    near-term discount factors. Then we use these to isolate later
    payments from coupon bonds. We repeat this until we’ve built the
    whole curve.

pages.title: 2.3. Interpolation: Fill in Gaps
pages.explainHtml:
节点之间需要插值（线性即期、线性 DF、对数 DF、样条等）。不同插值会改变中间期限的远期利率平滑度。

线性插值即期利率假设曲率为零，可能造成远期不稳定；这是作业里常见的「插值 vs 直接 bootstrap」对比点。

易错点：插值只是假设，不是市场真相；换插值方法，中间券的模型价可能跳几个 bp。
pages.excerpt:
2.3. Interpolation: Fill in Gaps
In practice, the yield curve needs to be estimated for all maturities — even
those for which we don’t have direct market data. Interpolation fills the gaps
between observed maturities.
The act of “filling in” is interpolation

pages.excerpt:
3.2. Spline Approximation of Discounts
Discussion: Where Should We Place the Knots?

Knots should match how the market works — not just where math feels nice.
Some research suggests:
• Shea (1984):
   Spread knots so each segment has about the same number of bonds.
   → Keeps data evenly distributed across the curve.
• Priaulet (1997): Use market-driven segments:
    – Short-term: 0–1 year (money market)
    – Medium: 1–7 years (active trading zone)
    – Long: 7–10 years
    – Very long: 10–30 years (less liquid, more volatile)
    These reflect how traders actually think — and help avoid big jumps in
forward rates.

Nelson-Siegel 用少数参数刻画水平、斜率、曲率成分，整条曲线参数化，稳健且便于比较不同日曲线。

y(τ) = β0 + β1·((1−e^{−λτ})/(λτ)) + β2·(((1−e^{−λτ})/(λτ)) − e^{−λτ})

扩展的 Svensson 模型再加一项，以捕捉更复杂的驼峰。参数有经济直觉，适合日常监控。

pages.excerpt:
Discussion
Just "Fitting the Curve Today" Isn’t Enough!
   It’s just a snapshot. It tells you nothing about how rates might change
tomorrow or next week. – no forecast power!

Most models (like spline or Nelson-Siegel) are static — they fit today’s data
well, but:
• They don’t tell us where rates are headed
• Their parameters (like hump size) change every day in unpredictable ways
• They don’t match well with dynamic models (like Hull-White)
   that do model how rates evolve over time.

So even if your model fits today perfectly, it won’t help much for pricing
options or managing risk going forward.

Quiz Questions
1. What is the fundamental principle behind the bootstrapping method
for deriving the yield curve?
A)Starting with short-term instruments to find near-term discount
factors, then using those to isolate and solve for longer-term rates
step-by-step. B) Averaging the yields of all bonds within a specific
maturity bucket.

2. What is a primary advantage of the Nelson-Siegel model over
simpler curve-fitting techniques?
A) It uses a very large number of parameters to perfectly fit every
single bond price. B) Its parameters (Level, Slope, Curvature) have
direct economic interpretations, making the model intuitive.

pages.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
pages.explainHtml:
总结页请当成考前速查卡：能用自己的话复述每一条，才算真懂。

对照左边要点，问自己：对应公式是什么？适用假设是什么？常见反例是什么？
pages.excerpt:
Summary & Key Takeaways

• Clean Data First: Filter bonds for a reliable, tradable basket.
  Remove outliers and complex bonds.
• Direct Way - Bootstrapping: Build the curve step-by-step
  from short to long rates. Use interpolation (e.g., splines) to
  fill gaps.
• Indirect Way - Smooth Fit: Fit one smooth curve to all
  data. Nelson-Siegel is key—its parameters
  mean Level, Slope, Curvature.
• Trade-off: Direct = precise but bumpy. Indirect = smooth
  but model risk. Neither predicts the future alone.
